en.headline: Lawmakers call for tighter safety rules after triathlon drowning
en.dek: Legislators urged organisers to introduce real-time tracking and clearer weather protocols following the death of a 59-year-old competitor during the swim leg at Tai Mei Tuk on Sunday.
body: Lawmakers on Monday called for immediate safety improvements in open-water events after a 59-year-old man died during the swimming segment of a triathlon held off Tai Mei Tuk in Tai Po on Sunday.

The competitor went missing during the race’s opening leg. Rescue teams later recovered him unconscious from the water and he was certified dead in hospital. Speaking on an RTHK programme, legislator Vincent Cheng said organisers already station rescue boats at intervals but suggested adding real-time GPS tracking that could alert officials if a participant fails to reach checkpoints within a set time.

Fellow lawmaker Adrian Ho highlighted the narrow rescue window in open water, noting that shifting weather, water temperature changes and sudden medical issues can quickly turn conditions dangerous. He proposed pairing GPS with artificial intelligence and underwater cameras to monitor athletes continuously and guide nearby rescuers. Both lawmakers said Hong Kong should study practices used overseas as extreme weather becomes more frequent.

zh.headline: 議員促三項鐵人賽加強安全措施
zh.dek: 立法會議員就周日大美督三項鐵人賽游泳項目有選手遇溺不治，促請主辦單位引入實時追蹤及更清晰的天氣指引。
body: 立法會議員周一就周日大埔大美督三項鐵人挑戰賽游泳項目有59歲男子遇溺不治，呼籲立即加強公開水域賽事安全措施。
該名選手於游泳階段失蹤，其後被救起時已昏迷，送院後證實死亡。議員鄭泳舜在電台節目表示，主辦單位已沿途部署救生船，但建議引入實時全球定位系統，若選手未能在指定時間內通過檢查點，可即時通知主辦單位。
議員何敬康指出公開水域救援窗口相對狹窄，天氣轉變、水溫下降或選手突然身體不適均可迅速令情況惡化。他建議結合全球定位、人工智能及水底鏡頭持續監察選手，並將位置即時傳予附近救生員。兩名議員均認為香港應參考其他地區做法，以應對更頻密的極端天氣。
